newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB debenture due Jan 99 traded at 7.0 pct-traders. [CORRECTED 02:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NCB debenture due Jan 99 traded at 7.0 pct-traders. [CORRECTED 02:00 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects the month in the headline and the text to January from November.)
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd's 1.4 percent debenture due January 1999 was traded at 7.0 percent on Friday morning, traders said.
Trade of the debentures amounted to about 200 million yen, they said.
"A few other NCB debentures with more than one year until maturity were traded at a yield of 7.0 percent this morning," said a dealer at a securities brokerage.

Traders said NCB debentures with a similar period until maturity were traded at around 8.0 percent on Thursday before the bank said later in the day that it expected to unveil a restructuring plan in early April.
NCB said it could not give a specific date for unveiling the plan until earnings results for the current business year ending March 31 became clearer.
The yield curve of NCB debentures has been flat for several weeks since they came under consistent selling pressure across the yield curve on fears over the bank's health.
Additional selling pressure appeared recently on fears that the government might not protect institutional investors in bank debentures if the issuer collapsed.

Moody's Investors Service on March 21 cut the rating on NCB's debentures to junk bond levels, saying it expected NCB might ultimately require outside assistance due to its massive problem loans. The rating was cut to Ba1 from Baa3.

Taku Yamasaki, chairman of the policy-making committee of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, said in a television programme last Sunday that bank debentures sold to institutional investors should not be protected by the use of public funds.
